Question B-008-001-003.

Why the correct answer is right: Interference that follows transmissions on any band is usually a receiver overload clue. A harmonic or spurious problem normally has a stronger relationship to particular frequencies.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Incorrect antenna length": A wrong antenna length affects the amateur station match and radiation, but it does not by itself explain a neighbour receiver reacting on every transmitting band.
- sourceIndex 2: "Spurious emissions": Spurious emissions are unwanted transmitter outputs; they usually show up at particular frequencies rather than the same way no matter which band is used.
- sourceIndex 3: "Deficient harmonic suppression": Poor harmonic suppression would tend to affect frequencies related to harmonics of the operating band, not produce the same symptom on all bands.
